The main takeaway from our work is that

the Gondwane basins formed in the African segment were not only controlled by the thermal subsidence of the Gondwanan lithosphere but also by the tectonic processes that affected the region during the Late Palaeozoico-Early Mesozoic.

the tectonic evolution of Gondwane was driven by a combination of processes, which include: (1) the formation of a supercontinent, (2) thermal subsidence, (3) subduction and (4) strike-slip tectonics.

the Late Palaeozoico to Early Mesozoico Gondwana basins are not related to a single event but to a series of tectonic and climatic changes that affected the supercontinent during a time span of about 100 million years.
